extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
extraction.description: A suite of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks for which prior language model evaluations did not outperform the average human-rater.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V . Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by filtering the existing BIG-Bench benchmark to identify tasks where the highest reported model performances were below the average human-rater score.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data comes from the BIG-Bench collaborative benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors applied a set of filtering criteria to BIG-Bench tasks, such as removing tasks with fewer than 103 examples, tasks without human-rater baselines, and tasks that do not use multiple-choice or exact match. For most tasks, a random subset of 250 evaluation examples was taken.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The authors manually composed three chain-of-thought exemplars for each task in the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The human-rater scores are not fully representative of human performance and should be interpreted with care. Surpassing average human-rater performance does not equate to true language understanding.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to be used as an evaluation suite to measure the capabilities of language models, specifically to facilitate further research on challenging tasks.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: BIG-Bench is a collaborative benchmark that aims to quantitatively measure the capabilities and limitations of language models (Srivastava et al., 2022, Beyond the Imitation GameBench mark).

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The above-mentioned factors suggest that the human-rater performance, as well as the results discussed in this work, should be interpreted with care.
